tagline.text: A bronze monument on the Tagbilaran shoreline recreating the 1565 blood compact

location.label: Location
location.text: Bool district, Tagbilaran City, Bohol (Venancio P. Inting Avenue / Tagbilaran East Road)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱100–300 (per person, tricycle round trip and snacks)

children.text: This monument recreates, in a bronze group, the 1565 blood compact in which the Bohol chieftain Sikatuna and the Spanish expedition leader Legazpi sealed their friendship. It is close to central Tagbilaran and free to enter, so it is a frequent first stop on Bohol tours, and it becomes far more interesting once you know the debate over whether this was the actual site of the ceremony.

The Blood Compact Shrine is a bronze sculpture monument standing by the seaside road in Bool district, Tagbilaran, the gateway city of Bohol. Locally it is called the Sandugo monument, in English the Blood Compact Shrine, and map apps list it as Blood Compact Site or Blood Pact Shrine. Sandugo means "one blood" in Visayan and refers to a pledge sealed by mixing the blood of two people.

The monument commemorates the blood compact made in 1565 between the Spanish expedition leader Miguel López de Legazpi and the Bohol chieftain Datu Sikatuna. Legazpi led an expedition that sailed from the port of Navidad in Mexico, and Sikatuna is said to have chosen the traditional blood oath rather than signing a document. In the ritual, the two men made small cuts, mixed their blood into wine, and shared the cup. It is commonly presented as the first friendship treaty between Filipinos and Spaniards. The date is given as
March 16
, and Republic Act 9093 set that day as Blood Compact Day in Bohol.

The sculpture is the work of the Bohol-born National Artist Napoleon Abueva. Five life-size bronze figures gather around a table to perform the ritual. The Bohol Strait opens up behind the figures, which makes for good photos, and a railed viewing area faces the sea. Information boards explain the meaning of Sandugo and give background on the sculptor.

There is one thing to know. Historians dispute whether this was where the compact actually took place. The former National Historical Institute delisted this Bool site in 2005, and its successor, the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP), places the real site in Hinawanan, Loay, east of here. So it is most accurate to visit the monument as a sculpture that remembers the event rather than as the event's actual location. Even so, it is a fixture of Bohol city tours, so stop briefly and add some history to the visit.

Five life-size bronze figures by the National Artist Napoleon Abueva gather around a table. They depict the moment Legazpi and Sikatuna share the cup, and you can see the faces and the folds of the clothing up close.
The sea opens up behind the sculpture, and there is a railed viewing area. In early morning or around sunset the light is soft, which suits silhouette photos of the figures.

blocks.title: The Sandugo story and information boards

children.text: Boards on site explain the meaning of Sandugo and the background of the ritual. Reading the story of friendship sealed with blood instead of a signature helps you understand the scene.

blocks.title: The question of the true site

children.text: The debate over whether Bool or Loay is the real site is part of what makes this monument interesting. Even the date differs, March 16 versus March 25, and local guides will give you different views.
The Sandugo Festival, held in Tagbilaran every
July
, honors this blood compact. During the festival, street dancing competitions and a re-enactment are held and the whole city comes alive.

There is no entrance fee, and it is about 10 minutes from downtown by tricycle, so it fits easily into a short gap. It works well as a first stop after arriving at the port or a last stop before heading to the airport.

blocks.title: Starting point of the countryside tour

children.text: Bohol day tours that loop through the Chocolate Hills, the tarsiers, and the Loboc River often start here or at Baclayon Church. It is usually included, so check the itinerary before booking.
Take a tricycle from downtown Tagbilaran or the port to the monument in Bool. It is close, usually about
10 minutes
away.
Read the information board in front of the bronze group and take photos. With five figures, walk around and change angles.
Rest at the seaside viewing area and look out over the Bohol Strait. Motorbikes and cars are loud along the road, so take photos when traffic is quiet.
Continue to
Baclayon Church
. Follow the same road east; it is reported to be about
10 minutes
by car.
After the church and museum, return to Tagbilaran for lunch.
The monument itself does not take long to see. It is more efficient to plan it together with other sights.

items.title: Easy first day
items.subtitle: A walk around town after the ferry

children.text: Arrive at Tagbilaran port and drop your bags at your hotel.
Take a tricycle to the monument and enjoy the sculpture and sea in the softer light.
Return to town for dinner at a seafood or local restaurant.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Bohol–Panglao International Airport (TAG), reported to be operated by Philippine Airlines, PAL Express, and Cebu Pacific. Flight time is about
1 hour 30 minutes
The airport is in Tawala on Panglao Island and opened in November 2018. Tagbilaran is on the main island across the water, so you need to travel from the airport by road.
Fares and flight frequencies change by season, so check airline apps.
From the airport to Tagbilaran, a taxi or booked car is reported to take about
20–30 minutes
. The exact time depends on traffic.
Fast craft from Cebu City Pier 1 to Tagbilaran port take about
2 hours
. OceanJet and others run several sailings a day.
Economy (tourist class) fares on OceanJet are
or so (announced June 2026, including a temporary fuel surcharge) and change with fuel prices, season, and operator. The slower RoRo ferry takes about
4–4.5 hours
and costs less.
A direct ship from Manila to Tagbilaran is reported to sail infrequently and take about
33 hours
, so most people fly or go via Cebu. Check the operator's latest schedule.

items.title: From downtown Tagbilaran to the monument

children.text: A tricycle is the easiest option. It is about
10 minutes
from the port or downtown, and fares are reported at about
, though sources differ widely.
In July 2026 the Tagbilaran mayor was reported to have signed an ordinance lowering the minimum tricycle fare to
, with
added per kilometer. The previous minimum was ₱20 and the start was expected July 27, but I found no report confirming it took effect. Confirm the actual fare with the driver before you ride.
Taxis, Grab, and rental cars also work. Say Blood Compact Shrine or Sandugo Shrine and drivers will understand.
It is included in most Bohol countryside tours. Check the stop list when you sign up for a tour.
Jeepneys and buses to Tagbilaran pass near the monument, but routes and stops change often, so ask the conductor to tell you where to get off.
The monument is an outdoor sculpture site, so weather matters. In the dry
November–May
season skies are clear, photos with the sea behind are good, and walking is comfortable.
Early morning or around sunset is best. At midday there is almost no shade and it is hot, and tour groups also crowd in then.
If you want to time your visit to an event, consider the
March 16
Blood Compact Day and the
July
Sandugo Festival period. The city is crowded then and lodging prices can rise.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Peak season, great for photos but tours and hotels are crowded
Strong midday sun, so go early in the morning or in the evening
Bring an umbrella for showers and leave time in your schedule

The area around the monument is a short roadside stop, so most visitors stay in downtown Tagbilaran or on Panglao Island. Tagbilaran is convenient, with the port and market close by and many budget and mid-range hotels. For a resort feel,
Panglao Island
with
Alona Beach
is popular, and it is reported to be about
30 minutes
by car from the monument.

It is best to eat in downtown Tagbilaran. Local markets and shops sell calamay, a Bohol sweet made from glutinous rice, and souvenir stalls are reported near the monument. Whether restaurants are open varies by season, so check locally. Restrooms and parking are said to be nearby, but facilities are basic, so do not expect much.
The monument itself takes 30 minutes at most. Combine it with
Baclayon Church
or a downtown schedule.
Go in early morning or around sunset for better photos and fewer people.
Knowing the NHCP position that this is not the actual ceremony site makes conversations with local guides richer.
If you are interested in Bohol history, also visit the Hinawanan marker in Loay to compare. It is reported to be about
17km
east of Tagbilaran.
Agree on the tricycle fare before boarding, and ask in advance whether you can find a ride back.
Travel sites list opening hours as
, but this is hard to confirm officially. The sculpture stands by the road and can be seen from outside, so if you arrive late, go anyway and check on site.
On a tour vehicle, stops are short. Tell your guide you want extra time to read the information boards after taking photos.

The NHCP has stated that this monument may not be where the compact actually took place. There has been discussion of relocating or reworking it; in March 2025 the DOT and the city held a groundbreaking for a Tourist Rest Area at the Friendship Park in Bool, and city plans to develop the park were reported again in March 2026. Construction progress and any access limits are unconfirmed, so check its current state before you visit.
Some travel sites say this structure was dismantled in 2024, but this is unconfirmed. Check local information before you go.
There is almost no shade and it is beside a road, so midday is hot and the traffic is loud. Bring a hat and water.
Watch for motorbikes and tricycles when crossing the road or taking photos.
As at any tourist spot, watch for pickpockets and wear your bag in front. You can politely decline souvenir sellers who approach you.
Fares, opening hours, and transport details can change, so check the latest announcements.
A Spanish-era stone church about
10 minutes
by car from the monument. On Bohol tours it is almost always paired with this stop.
The gateway city of Bohol, with the port, markets, and restaurants. The monument is about
3km
from the city center.
A river cruise attraction about
40 minutes
by car from Tagbilaran. It is known for its floating lunch.
A resort island about
30 minutes
by car from the monument, with beaches and diving bases.
The place the NHCP regards as the real blood compact site, east of Tagbilaran. It is worth a visit as a comparison trip for history fans; check locally on the current state of development.
